legacy_reasons: KMHFR provides official facility records with constituency location and can support constituency facility counts. A facility count is not relabelled as a population density, and no county/sub-county population is inherited downward.

rows.audit_note: P28A requires this legacy omission/closure to be re-opened under the S2/S3/S4/S5 fallback hierarchy before S6 can be treated as the successor disposition.
legacy_reasons: Narok is explicitly shown without a pending-bills amount in the final Table 10 county breakdown because the entity did not submit pending-bills data. The Atlas preserves this as official non-submission; it is not zero and is not reverse-engineered from the budget percentage column.

rows.current_source_label: Ministry of Health — Kenya Master Health Facility Registry (KMHFR)
rows.audit_note: P28A requires this legacy omission/closure to be re-opened under the S2/S3/S4/S5 fallback hierarchy before S6 can be treated as the successor disposition.
legacy_reasons: The Atlas attempted to resolve this indicator at ward level via spatial_derivation: a point-in-polygon count of geocoded, operational KMHFR facilities against the Atlas's own canonical 1,450-ward polygon layer (data/geography/geometry/wards.geojson), divided by a ward population denominator. Both the public KMHFR facility portal and its documented GIS/API host were unreachable from the build environment on repeated attempts on 2026-09-08 (DNS resolved; every TCP connection over HTTP and HTTPS timed out or was refused), while the Ministry's own health.go.ke apex domain was reachable at the same time, showing this is a targeted access failure rather than a general outage. A systematic search for a genuine alternative official geocoded facility list found none that qualifies: the only official KMHFR-derived extract available for download (HDX "Kenya - Health facilities in Kenya", 2017) has no latitude/longitude field at all and is a 2017 snapshot of 8,932 facilities that predates and does not reconcile to the 2023 Kenya Health Facility Census total (14,883 facilities) already anchoring this indicator at county level; the only current, geocoded facility datasets found (healthsites.io's "Kenya Healthsites" export and the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team's "Health Facilities of Kenya" export) are both built from OpenStreetMap volunteer mapping rather than an official government registry and both self-disclose incomplete, geographically uneven coverage, so neither can support a Class C spatially-derived observation under the Atlas data-quality framework, which requires a documented official input for that class. Independently, the ward population denominator required for a facilities-per-10,000-residents rate does not yet exist in the canonical registry (IND-POPULATION currently resolves only to country and county level). A facility count is not relabelled as a population density, and no county or constituency value is inherited downward to any ward.

rows.current_source_label: KNBS — 2019 Kenya Population and Housing Census Reports (Volumes I–IV)
rows.audit_note: P28A requires this legacy omission/closure to be re-opened under the S2/S3/S4/S5 fallback hierarchy before S6 can be treated as the successor disposition.
legacy_reasons: KNBS's 2019 KPHC report series (Volumes I–IV) does not publish population as a direct table for the current 1,450 IEBC county assembly wards; its finest published administrative tier is the sub-location, which is a different, non-coterminous geography from the electoral ward. The IEBC boundary-delimitation exercise that would have produced an official ward population table was never completed or gazetted. No authoritative crosswalk exists to aggregate published sub-location (or any coarser KNBS unit) counts into the 1,450 current wards, so no genuine ward-level published figure can be attached without fabricating one.

legacy_reasons: The Atlas attempted to resolve this indicator at ward level via spatial_derivation: a point-in-polygon count of geocoded, operational KMHFR facilities against the Atlas's own canonical 1,450-ward polygon layer (data/geography/geometry/wards.geojson), divided by a ward population denominator. Both the public KMHFR facility portal and its documented GIS/API host were unreachable from the build environment on repeated attempts on 2026-09-08 (DNS resolved; every TCP connection over HTTP and HTTPS timed out or was refused), while the Ministry's own health.go.ke apex domain was reachable at the same time, showing this is a targeted access failure rather than a general outage. A systematic search for a genuine alternative official geocoded facility list found none that qualifies: the only official KMHFR-derived extract available for download (HDX "Kenya - Health facilities in Kenya", 2017) has no latitude/longitude field at all and is a 2017 snapshot of 8,932 facilities that predates and does not reconcile to the 2023 Kenya Health Facility Census total (14,883 facilities) already anchoring this indicator at county level; the only current, geocoded facility datasets found (healthsites.io's "Kenya Healthsites" export and the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team's "Health Facilities of Kenya" export) are both built from OpenStreetMap volunteer mapping rather than an official government registry and both self-disclose incomplete, geographically uneven coverage, so neither can support a Class C spatially-derived observation under the Atlas data-quality framework, which requires a documented official input for that class. Independently, the ward population denominator required for a facilities-per-10,000-residents rate does not yet exist in the canonical registry (IND-POPULATION currently resolves only to country and county level). A facility count is not relabelled as a population density, and no county or constituency value is inherited downward to any ward.

legacy_reasons: The Atlas attempted to resolve this indicator at ward level via spatial_derivation: a point-in-polygon count of geocoded, operational KMHFR facilities against the Atlas's own canonical 1,450-ward polygon layer (data/geography/geometry/wards.geojson), divided by a ward population denominator. Both the public KMHFR facility portal and its documented GIS/API host were unreachable from the build environment on repeated attempts on 2026-09-08 (DNS resolved; every TCP connection over HTTP and HTTPS timed out or was refused), while the Ministry's own health.go.ke apex domain was reachable at the same time, showing this is a targeted access failure rather than a general outage. A systematic search for a genuine alternative official geocoded facility list found none that qualifies: the only official KMHFR-derived extract available for download (HDX "Kenya - Health facilities in Kenya", 2017) has no latitude/longitude field at all and is a 2017 snapshot of 8,932 facilities that predates and does not reconcile to the 2023 Kenya Health Facility Census total (14,883 facilities) already anchoring this indicator at county level; the only current, geocoded facility datasets found (healthsites.io's "Kenya Healthsites" export and the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team's "Health Facilities of Kenya" export) are both built from OpenStreetMap volunteer mapping rather than an official government registry and both self-disclose incomplete, geographically uneven coverage, so neither can support a Class C spatially-derived observation under the Atlas data-quality framework, which requires a documented official input for that class. Independently, the ward population denominator required for a facilities-per-10,000-residents rate does not yet exist in the canonical registry (IND-POPULATION currently resolves only to country and county level). A facility count is not relabelled as a population density, and no county or constituency value is inherited downward to any ward.

legacy_reasons: The Atlas attempted to resolve this indicator at ward level via spatial_derivation: a point-in-polygon count of geocoded, operational KMHFR facilities against the Atlas's own canonical 1,450-ward polygon layer (data/geography/geometry/wards.geojson), divided by a ward population denominator. Both the public KMHFR facility portal and its documented GIS/API host were unreachable from the build environment on repeated attempts on 2026-09-08 (DNS resolved; every TCP connection over HTTP and HTTPS timed out or was refused), while the Ministry's own health.go.ke apex domain was reachable at the same time, showing this is a targeted access failure rather than a general outage. A systematic search for a genuine alternative official geocoded facility list found none that qualifies: the only official KMHFR-derived extract available for download (HDX "Kenya - Health facilities in Kenya", 2017) has no latitude/longitude field at all and is a 2017 snapshot of 8,932 facilities that predates and does not reconcile to the 2023 Kenya Health Facility Census total (14,883 facilities) already anchoring this indicator at county level; the only current, geocoded facility datasets found (healthsites.io's "Kenya Healthsites" export and the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team's "Health Facilities of Kenya" export) are both built from OpenStreetMap volunteer mapping rather than an official government registry and both self-disclose incomplete, geographically uneven coverage, so neither can support a Class C spatially-derived observation under the Atlas data-quality framework, which requires a documented official input for that class. Independently, the ward population denominator required for a facilities-per-10,000-residents rate does not yet exist in the canonical registry (IND-POPULATION currently resolves only to country and county level). A facility count is not relabelled as a population density, and no county or constituency value is inherited downward to any ward.

legacy_reasons: The Atlas attempted to resolve this indicator at ward level via spatial_derivation: a point-in-polygon count of geocoded, operational KMHFR facilities against the Atlas's own canonical 1,450-ward polygon layer (data/geography/geometry/wards.geojson), divided by a ward population denominator. Both the public KMHFR facility portal and its documented GIS/API host were unreachable from the build environment on repeated attempts on 2026-09-08 (DNS resolved; every TCP connection over HTTP and HTTPS timed out or was refused), while the Ministry's own health.go.ke apex domain was reachable at the same time, showing this is a targeted access failure rather than a general outage. A systematic search for a genuine alternative official geocoded facility list found none that qualifies: the only official KMHFR-derived extract available for download (HDX "Kenya - Health facilities in Kenya", 2017) has no latitude/longitude field at all and is a 2017 snapshot of 8,932 facilities that predates and does not reconcile to the 2023 Kenya Health Facility Census total (14,883 facilities) already anchoring this indicator at county level; the only current, geocoded facility datasets found (healthsites.io's "Kenya Healthsites" export and the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team's "Health Facilities of Kenya" export) are both built from OpenStreetMap volunteer mapping rather than an official government registry and both self-disclose incomplete, geographically uneven coverage, so neither can support a Class C spatially-derived observation under the Atlas data-quality framework, which requires a documented official input for that class. Independently, the ward population denominator required for a facilities-per-10,000-residents rate does not yet exist in the canonical registry (IND-POPULATION currently resolves only to country and county level). A facility count is not relabelled as a population density, and no county or constituency value is inherited downward to any ward.

legacy_reasons: The Atlas attempted to resolve this indicator at ward level via spatial_derivation: a point-in-polygon count of geocoded, operational KMHFR facilities against the Atlas's own canonical 1,450-ward polygon layer (data/geography/geometry/wards.geojson), divided by a ward population denominator. Both the public KMHFR facility portal and its documented GIS/API host were unreachable from the build environment on repeated attempts on 2026-09-08 (DNS resolved; every TCP connection over HTTP and HTTPS timed out or was refused), while the Ministry's own health.go.ke apex domain was reachable at the same time, showing this is a targeted access failure rather than a general outage. A systematic search for a genuine alternative official geocoded facility list found none that qualifies: the only official KMHFR-derived extract available for download (HDX "Kenya - Health facilities in Kenya", 2017) has no latitude/longitude field at all and is a 2017 snapshot of 8,932 facilities that predates and does not reconcile to the 2023 Kenya Health Facility Census total (14,883 facilities) already anchoring this indicator at county level; the only current, geocoded facility datasets found (healthsites.io's "Kenya Healthsites" export and the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team's "Health Facilities of Kenya" export) are both built from OpenStreetMap volunteer mapping rather than an official government registry and both self-disclose incomplete, geographically uneven coverage, so neither can support a Class C spatially-derived observation under the Atlas data-quality framework, which requires a documented official input for that class. Independently, the ward population denominator required for a facilities-per-10,000-residents rate does not yet exist in the canonical registry (IND-POPULATION currently resolves only to country and county level). A facility count is not relabelled as a population density, and no county or constituency value is inherited downward to any ward.

legacy_reasons: The Atlas attempted to resolve this indicator at ward level via spatial_derivation: a point-in-polygon count of geocoded, operational KMHFR facilities against the Atlas's own canonical 1,450-ward polygon layer (data/geography/geometry/wards.geojson), divided by a ward population denominator. Both the public KMHFR facility portal and its documented GIS/API host were unreachable from the build environment on repeated attempts on 2026-09-08 (DNS resolved; every TCP connection over HTTP and HTTPS timed out or was refused), while the Ministry's own health.go.ke apex domain was reachable at the same time, showing this is a targeted access failure rather than a general outage. A systematic search for a genuine alternative official geocoded facility list found none that qualifies: the only official KMHFR-derived extract available for download (HDX "Kenya - Health facilities in Kenya", 2017) has no latitude/longitude field at all and is a 2017 snapshot of 8,932 facilities that predates and does not reconcile to the 2023 Kenya Health Facility Census total (14,883 facilities) already anchoring this indicator at county level; the only current, geocoded facility datasets found (healthsites.io's "Kenya Healthsites" export and the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team's "Health Facilities of Kenya" export) are both built from OpenStreetMap volunteer mapping rather than an official government registry and both self-disclose incomplete, geographically uneven coverage, so neither can support a Class C spatially-derived observation under the Atlas data-quality framework, which requires a documented official input for that class. Independently, the ward population denominator required for a facilities-per-10,000-residents rate does not yet exist in the canonical registry (IND-POPULATION currently resolves only to country and county level). A facility count is not relabelled as a population density, and no county or constituency value is inherited downward to any ward.

legacy_reasons: The Atlas attempted to resolve this indicator at ward level via spatial_derivation: a point-in-polygon count of geocoded, operational KMHFR facilities against the Atlas's own canonical 1,450-ward polygon layer (data/geography/geometry/wards.geojson), divided by a ward population denominator. Both the public KMHFR facility portal and its documented GIS/API host were unreachable from the build environment on repeated attempts on 2026-09-08 (DNS resolved; every TCP connection over HTTP and HTTPS timed out or was refused), while the Ministry's own health.go.ke apex domain was reachable at the same time, showing this is a targeted access failure rather than a general outage. A systematic search for a genuine alternative official geocoded facility list found none that qualifies: the only official KMHFR-derived extract available for download (HDX "Kenya - Health facilities in Kenya", 2017) has no latitude/longitude field at all and is a 2017 snapshot of 8,932 facilities that predates and does not reconcile to the 2023 Kenya Health Facility Census total (14,883 facilities) already anchoring this indicator at county level; the only current, geocoded facility datasets found (healthsites.io's "Kenya Healthsites" export and the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team's "Health Facilities of Kenya" export) are both built from OpenStreetMap volunteer mapping rather than an official government registry and both self-disclose incomplete, geographically uneven coverage, so neither can support a Class C spatially-derived observation under the Atlas data-quality framework, which requires a documented official input for that class. Independently, the ward population denominator required for a facilities-per-10,000-residents rate does not yet exist in the canonical registry (IND-POPULATION currently resolves only to country and county level). A facility count is not relabelled as a population density, and no county or constituency value is inherited downward to any ward.

legacy_reasons: The Atlas attempted to resolve this indicator at ward level via spatial_derivation: a point-in-polygon count of geocoded, operational KMHFR facilities against the Atlas's own canonical 1,450-ward polygon layer (data/geography/geometry/wards.geojson), divided by a ward population denominator. Both the public KMHFR facility portal and its documented GIS/API host were unreachable from the build environment on repeated attempts on 2026-09-08 (DNS resolved; every TCP connection over HTTP and HTTPS timed out or was refused), while the Ministry's own health.go.ke apex domain was reachable at the same time, showing this is a targeted access failure rather than a general outage. A systematic search for a genuine alternative official geocoded facility list found none that qualifies: the only official KMHFR-derived extract available for download (HDX "Kenya - Health facilities in Kenya", 2017) has no latitude/longitude field at all and is a 2017 snapshot of 8,932 facilities that predates and does not reconcile to the 2023 Kenya Health Facility Census total (14,883 facilities) already anchoring this indicator at county level; the only current, geocoded facility datasets found (healthsites.io's "Kenya Healthsites" export and the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team's "Health Facilities of Kenya" export) are both built from OpenStreetMap volunteer mapping rather than an official government registry and both self-disclose incomplete, geographically uneven coverage, so neither can support a Class C spatially-derived observation under the Atlas data-quality framework, which requires a documented official input for that class. Independently, the ward population denominator required for a facilities-per-10,000-residents rate does not yet exist in the canonical registry (IND-POPULATION currently resolves only to country and county level). A facility count is not relabelled as a population density, and no county or constituency value is inherited downward to any ward.

legacy_reasons: The Atlas attempted to resolve this indicator at ward level via spatial_derivation: a point-in-polygon count of geocoded, operational KMHFR facilities against the Atlas's own canonical 1,450-ward polygon layer (data/geography/geometry/wards.geojson), divided by a ward population denominator. Both the public KMHFR facility portal and its documented GIS/API host were unreachable from the build environment on repeated attempts on 2026-09-08 (DNS resolved; every TCP connection over HTTP and HTTPS timed out or was refused), while the Ministry's own health.go.ke apex domain was reachable at the same time, showing this is a targeted access failure rather than a general outage. A systematic search for a genuine alternative official geocoded facility list found none that qualifies: the only official KMHFR-derived extract available for download (HDX "Kenya - Health facilities in Kenya", 2017) has no latitude/longitude field at all and is a 2017 snapshot of 8,932 facilities that predates and does not reconcile to the 2023 Kenya Health Facility Census total (14,883 facilities) already anchoring this indicator at county level; the only current, geocoded facility datasets found (healthsites.io's "Kenya Healthsites" export and the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team's "Health Facilities of Kenya" export) are both built from OpenStreetMap volunteer mapping rather than an official government registry and both self-disclose incomplete, geographically uneven coverage, so neither can support a Class C spatially-derived observation under the Atlas data-quality framework, which requires a documented official input for that class. Independently, the ward population denominator required for a facilities-per-10,000-residents rate does not yet exist in the canonical registry (IND-POPULATION currently resolves only to country and county level). A facility count is not relabelled as a population density, and no county or constituency value is inherited downward to any ward.

legacy_reasons: The Atlas attempted to resolve this indicator at ward level via spatial_derivation: a point-in-polygon count of geocoded, operational KMHFR facilities against the Atlas's own canonical 1,450-ward polygon layer (data/geography/geometry/wards.geojson), divided by a ward population denominator. Both the public KMHFR facility portal and its documented GIS/API host were unreachable from the build environment on repeated attempts on 2026-09-08 (DNS resolved; every TCP connection over HTTP and HTTPS timed out or was refused), while the Ministry's own health.go.ke apex domain was reachable at the same time, showing this is a targeted access failure rather than a general outage. A systematic search for a genuine alternative official geocoded facility list found none that qualifies: the only official KMHFR-derived extract available for download (HDX "Kenya - Health facilities in Kenya", 2017) has no latitude/longitude field at all and is a 2017 snapshot of 8,932 facilities that predates and does not reconcile to the 2023 Kenya Health Facility Census total (14,883 facilities) already anchoring this indicator at county level; the only current, geocoded facility datasets found (healthsites.io's "Kenya Healthsites" export and the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team's "Health Facilities of Kenya" export) are both built from OpenStreetMap volunteer mapping rather than an official government registry and both self-disclose incomplete, geographically uneven coverage, so neither can support a Class C spatially-derived observation under the Atlas data-quality framework, which requires a documented official input for that class. Independently, the ward population denominator required for a facilities-per-10,000-residents rate does not yet exist in the canonical registry (IND-POPULATION currently resolves only to country and county level). A facility count is not relabelled as a population density, and no county or constituency value is inherited downward to any ward.

legacy_reasons: The Atlas attempted to resolve this indicator at ward level via spatial_derivation: a point-in-polygon count of geocoded, operational KMHFR facilities against the Atlas's own canonical 1,450-ward polygon layer (data/geography/geometry/wards.geojson), divided by a ward population denominator. Both the public KMHFR facility portal and its documented GIS/API host were unreachable from the build environment on repeated attempts on 2026-09-08 (DNS resolved; every TCP connection over HTTP and HTTPS timed out or was refused), while the Ministry's own health.go.ke apex domain was reachable at the same time, showing this is a targeted access failure rather than a general outage. A systematic search for a genuine alternative official geocoded facility list found none that qualifies: the only official KMHFR-derived extract available for download (HDX "Kenya - Health facilities in Kenya", 2017) has no latitude/longitude field at all and is a 2017 snapshot of 8,932 facilities that predates and does not reconcile to the 2023 Kenya Health Facility Census total (14,883 facilities) already anchoring this indicator at county level; the only current, geocoded facility datasets found (healthsites.io's "Kenya Healthsites" export and the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team's "Health Facilities of Kenya" export) are both built from OpenStreetMap volunteer mapping rather than an official government registry and both self-disclose incomplete, geographically uneven coverage, so neither can support a Class C spatially-derived observation under the Atlas data-quality framework, which requires a documented official input for that class. Independently, the ward population denominator required for a facilities-per-10,000-residents rate does not yet exist in the canonical registry (IND-POPULATION currently resolves only to country and county level). A facility count is not relabelled as a population density, and no county or constituency value is inherited downward to any ward.

legacy_reasons: The Atlas attempted to resolve this indicator at ward level via spatial_derivation: a point-in-polygon count of geocoded, operational KMHFR facilities against the Atlas's own canonical 1,450-ward polygon layer (data/geography/geometry/wards.geojson), divided by a ward population denominator. Both the public KMHFR facility portal and its documented GIS/API host were unreachable from the build environment on repeated attempts on 2026-09-08 (DNS resolved; every TCP connection over HTTP and HTTPS timed out or was refused), while the Ministry's own health.go.ke apex domain was reachable at the same time, showing this is a targeted access failure rather than a general outage. A systematic search for a genuine alternative official geocoded facility list found none that qualifies: the only official KMHFR-derived extract available for download (HDX "Kenya - Health facilities in Kenya", 2017) has no latitude/longitude field at all and is a 2017 snapshot of 8,932 facilities that predates and does not reconcile to the 2023 Kenya Health Facility Census total (14,883 facilities) already anchoring this indicator at county level; the only current, geocoded facility datasets found (healthsites.io's "Kenya Healthsites" export and the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team's "Health Facilities of Kenya" export) are both built from OpenStreetMap volunteer mapping rather than an official government registry and both self-disclose incomplete, geographically uneven coverage, so neither can support a Class C spatially-derived observation under the Atlas data-quality framework, which requires a documented official input for that class. Independently, the ward population denominator required for a facilities-per-10,000-residents rate does not yet exist in the canonical registry (IND-POPULATION currently resolves only to country and county level). A facility count is not relabelled as a population density, and no county or constituency value is inherited downward to any ward.

legacy_reasons: The Atlas attempted to resolve this indicator at ward level via spatial_derivation: a point-in-polygon count of geocoded, operational KMHFR facilities against the Atlas's own canonical 1,450-ward polygon layer (data/geography/geometry/wards.geojson), divided by a ward population denominator. Both the public KMHFR facility portal and its documented GIS/API host were unreachable from the build environment on repeated attempts on 2026-09-08 (DNS resolved; every TCP connection over HTTP and HTTPS timed out or was refused), while the Ministry's own health.go.ke apex domain was reachable at the same time, showing this is a targeted access failure rather than a general outage. A systematic search for a genuine alternative official geocoded facility list found none that qualifies: the only official KMHFR-derived extract available for download (HDX "Kenya - Health facilities in Kenya", 2017) has no latitude/longitude field at all and is a 2017 snapshot of 8,932 facilities that predates and does not reconcile to the 2023 Kenya Health Facility Census total (14,883 facilities) already anchoring this indicator at county level; the only current, geocoded facility datasets found (healthsites.io's "Kenya Healthsites" export and the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team's "Health Facilities of Kenya" export) are both built from OpenStreetMap volunteer mapping rather than an official government registry and both self-disclose incomplete, geographically uneven coverage, so neither can support a Class C spatially-derived observation under the Atlas data-quality framework, which requires a documented official input for that class. Independently, the ward population denominator required for a facilities-per-10,000-residents rate does not yet exist in the canonical registry (IND-POPULATION currently resolves only to country and county level). A facility count is not relabelled as a population density, and no county or constituency value is inherited downward to any ward.

legacy_reasons: The Atlas attempted to resolve this indicator at ward level via spatial_derivation: a point-in-polygon count of geocoded, operational KMHFR facilities against the Atlas's own canonical 1,450-ward polygon layer (data/geography/geometry/wards.geojson), divided by a ward population denominator. Both the public KMHFR facility portal and its documented GIS/API host were unreachable from the build environment on repeated attempts on 2026-09-08 (DNS resolved; every TCP connection over HTTP and HTTPS timed out or was refused), while the Ministry's own health.go.ke apex domain was reachable at the same time, showing this is a targeted access failure rather than a general outage. A systematic search for a genuine alternative official geocoded facility list found none that qualifies: the only official KMHFR-derived extract available for download (HDX "Kenya - Health facilities in Kenya", 2017) has no latitude/longitude field at all and is a 2017 snapshot of 8,932 facilities that predates and does not reconcile to the 2023 Kenya Health Facility Census total (14,883 facilities) already anchoring this indicator at county level; the only current, geocoded facility datasets found (healthsites.io's "Kenya Healthsites" export and the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team's "Health Facilities of Kenya" export) are both built from OpenStreetMap volunteer mapping rather than an official government registry and both self-disclose incomplete, geographically uneven coverage, so neither can support a Class C spatially-derived observation under the Atlas data-quality framework, which requires a documented official input for that class. Independently, the ward population denominator required for a facilities-per-10,000-residents rate does not yet exist in the canonical registry (IND-POPULATION currently resolves only to country and county level). A facility count is not relabelled as a population density, and no county or constituency value is inherited downward to any ward.

legacy_reasons: The Atlas attempted to resolve this indicator at ward level via spatial_derivation: a point-in-polygon count of geocoded, operational KMHFR facilities against the Atlas's own canonical 1,450-ward polygon layer (data/geography/geometry/wards.geojson), divided by a ward population denominator. Both the public KMHFR facility portal and its documented GIS/API host were unreachable from the build environment on repeated attempts on 2026-09-08 (DNS resolved; every TCP connection over HTTP and HTTPS timed out or was refused), while the Ministry's own health.go.ke apex domain was reachable at the same time, showing this is a targeted access failure rather than a general outage. A systematic search for a genuine alternative official geocoded facility list found none that qualifies: the only official KMHFR-derived extract available for download (HDX "Kenya - Health facilities in Kenya", 2017) has no latitude/longitude field at all and is a 2017 snapshot of 8,932 facilities that predates and does not reconcile to the 2023 Kenya Health Facility Census total (14,883 facilities) already anchoring this indicator at county level; the only current, geocoded facility datasets found (healthsites.io's "Kenya Healthsites" export and the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team's "Health Facilities of Kenya" export) are both built from OpenStreetMap volunteer mapping rather than an official government registry and both self-disclose incomplete, geographically uneven coverage, so neither can support a Class C spatially-derived observation under the Atlas data-quality framework, which requires a documented official input for that class. Independently, the ward population denominator required for a facilities-per-10,000-residents rate does not yet exist in the canonical registry (IND-POPULATION currently resolves only to country and county level). A facility count is not relabelled as a population density, and no county or constituency value is inherited downward to any ward.

legacy_reasons: The Atlas attempted to resolve this indicator at ward level via spatial_derivation: a point-in-polygon count of geocoded, operational KMHFR facilities against the Atlas's own canonical 1,450-ward polygon layer (data/geography/geometry/wards.geojson), divided by a ward population denominator. Both the public KMHFR facility portal and its documented GIS/API host were unreachable from the build environment on repeated attempts on 2026-09-08 (DNS resolved; every TCP connection over HTTP and HTTPS timed out or was refused), while the Ministry's own health.go.ke apex domain was reachable at the same time, showing this is a targeted access failure rather than a general outage. A systematic search for a genuine alternative official geocoded facility list found none that qualifies: the only official KMHFR-derived extract available for download (HDX "Kenya - Health facilities in Kenya", 2017) has no latitude/longitude field at all and is a 2017 snapshot of 8,932 facilities that predates and does not reconcile to the 2023 Kenya Health Facility Census total (14,883 facilities) already anchoring this indicator at county level; the only current, geocoded facility datasets found (healthsites.io's "Kenya Healthsites" export and the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team's "Health Facilities of Kenya" export) are both built from OpenStreetMap volunteer mapping rather than an official government registry and both self-disclose incomplete, geographically uneven coverage, so neither can support a Class C spatially-derived observation under the Atlas data-quality framework, which requires a documented official input for that class. Independently, the ward population denominator required for a facilities-per-10,000-residents rate does not yet exist in the canonical registry (IND-POPULATION currently resolves only to country and county level). A facility count is not relabelled as a population density, and no county or constituency value is inherited downward to any ward.

legacy_reasons: The Atlas attempted to resolve this indicator at ward level via spatial_derivation: a point-in-polygon count of geocoded, operational KMHFR facilities against the Atlas's own canonical 1,450-ward polygon layer (data/geography/geometry/wards.geojson), divided by a ward population denominator. Both the public KMHFR facility portal and its documented GIS/API host were unreachable from the build environment on repeated attempts on 2026-09-08 (DNS resolved; every TCP connection over HTTP and HTTPS timed out or was refused), while the Ministry's own health.go.ke apex domain was reachable at the same time, showing this is a targeted access failure rather than a general outage. A systematic search for a genuine alternative official geocoded facility list found none that qualifies: the only official KMHFR-derived extract available for download (HDX "Kenya - Health facilities in Kenya", 2017) has no latitude/longitude field at all and is a 2017 snapshot of 8,932 facilities that predates and does not reconcile to the 2023 Kenya Health Facility Census total (14,883 facilities) already anchoring this indicator at county level; the only current, geocoded facility datasets found (healthsites.io's "Kenya Healthsites" export and the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team's "Health Facilities of Kenya" export) are both built from OpenStreetMap volunteer mapping rather than an official government registry and both self-disclose incomplete, geographically uneven coverage, so neither can support a Class C spatially-derived observation under the Atlas data-quality framework, which requires a documented official input for that class. Independently, the ward population denominator required for a facilities-per-10,000-residents rate does not yet exist in the canonical registry (IND-POPULATION currently resolves only to country and county level). A facility count is not relabelled as a population density, and no county or constituency value is inherited downward to any ward.

rows.current_source_label: IEBC Gazette Notice No. 7290 — Registered Voters per County Assembly Ward (First Schedule); Kenya Data Atlas P23X ward-voter materialisation (scripts/p23/build-ward-voters.mjs, data/sprint2/README.md)
rows.audit_note: P28A requires this legacy omission/closure to be re-opened under the S2/S3/S4/S5 fallback hierarchy before S6 can be treated as the successor disposition.
legacy_reasons: The Kenya Data Atlas already materialises registered-voter counts for 1,440 of the 1,450 statistical wards directly from IEBC Gazette Notice No. 7290 (scripts/p23/build-ward-voters.mjs). Ten official source rows across two constituencies remain withheld from canonical ward geometry: Mandera East (constituency 43 — Arabia, Bulla Mpya, Khalalio, Neboi, Township) and Lafey (constituency 44 — Libehia, Fino, Lafey, Warankara, Alungo Gof). The current externally sourced ward boundary layer for this pair of constituencies conflicts with the operative IEBC configuration, so a safe deterministic one-to-one crosswalk between the ten official CAW source rows and the ten canonical ward polygons cannot be established without risking a false attribution of a specific voter count to the wrong ward. This is the same documented Mandera East/Lafey spatial hold referenced throughout the Atlas (CHANGELOG.md; docs/DATA-COMPLETION-PLAN.md, Track B and the P24 acceptance criteria) and deliberately preserved through the P23A/P23X constituency and ward voter materialisation: the ten source rows remain correctly included in the Mandera East and Lafey constituency-level totals as an exact aggregation of all official First Schedule child-ward rows, but are not force-matched, interpolated, or evenly split across the five ward polygons in either constituency at the ward level. The ward-level completeness ledger slot for these ten wards is therefore closed as boundary unresolved — a genuine geometry/crosswalk constraint distinct from data non-publication — rather than left as an unexplained blank or filled with a fabricated or force-matched value.

rows.current_source_label: Ministry of Health — Kenya Master Health Facility Registry (KMHFR)
rows.audit_note: P28A requires this legacy omission/closure to be re-opened under the S2/S3/S4/S5 fallback hierarchy before S6 can be treated as the successor disposition.
legacy_reasons: The Atlas attempted to resolve this indicator at ward level via spatial_derivation: a point-in-polygon count of geocoded, operational KMHFR facilities against the Atlas's own canonical 1,450-ward polygon layer (data/geography/geometry/wards.geojson), divided by a ward population denominator. Both the public KMHFR facility portal and its documented GIS/API host were unreachable from the build environment on repeated attempts on 2026-09-08 (DNS resolved; every TCP connection over HTTP and HTTPS timed out or was refused), while the Ministry's own health.go.ke apex domain was reachable at the same time, showing this is a targeted access failure rather than a general outage. A systematic search for a genuine alternative official geocoded facility list found none that qualifies: the only official KMHFR-derived extract available for download (HDX "Kenya - Health facilities in Kenya", 2017) has no latitude/longitude field at all and is a 2017 snapshot of 8,932 facilities that predates and does not reconcile to the 2023 Kenya Health Facility Census total (14,883 facilities) already anchoring this indicator at county level; the only current, geocoded facility datasets found (healthsites.io's "Kenya Healthsites" export and the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team's "Health Facilities of Kenya" export) are both built from OpenStreetMap volunteer mapping rather than an official government registry and both self-disclose incomplete, geographically uneven coverage, so neither can support a Class C spatially-derived observation under the Atlas data-quality framework, which requires a documented official input for that class. Independently, the ward population denominator required for a facilities-per-10,000-residents rate does not yet exist in the canonical registry (IND-POPULATION currently resolves only to country and county level). A facility count is not relabelled as a population density, and no county or constituency value is inherited downward to any ward.
